inventory.name: Series N700S Shinkansen
inventory.claim: JR Central records the launch of its Supreme Class Cabin service. The operator identifies the 16-car N700S as the fleet for that service between Tokyo and Hakata. Initial N700S passenger service on the Tōkaidō line began on 1 July 2020.
inventory.limit: The October milestone applies to equipped N700S trainsets. It establishes continued use of the type without giving a fleet census or a record of individual trips through the cutoff date.

inventory.name: Taiwan High Speed Rail 700T
inventory.claim: THSRC reported deploying its existing 34 trainsets during the September holiday peak while the next-generation trainsets were in safety tests. A separate operator notice identifies the existing type as 700T. The type entered passenger service on 5 January 2007.
inventory.limit: The deployment is for the September holiday peak. The source does not list individual trip assignments.

inventory.claim: THSRC says its first N700ST reached 170 km/h in its first main-line test while checking compatibility with the track and overhead power.
inventory.limit: The run was a trial. The operator scheduled passenger service from 1 July 2027, subject to the remaining tests and entry requirements.

trace: The Taiwan N700ST adapted JR Central’s N700S for the receiving operator’s route and service. The manufacturer and Taiwan High Speed Rail document the transfer and localization (taiwan-high-speed-rail-n700st → shinkansen-series-n700s).

The Series N700S combined silicon-carbide electronics with the train-draft cooling used by some Series N700 converters. A Series N700 train also served as a test platform for prototype equipment. The N700, in turn, developed the Series 700 basis, expanding semi-active vibration control to all cars (shinkansen-series-n700s → shinkansen-series-n700 → shinkansen-series-700). JR Central’s technical history also identifies N700A as a February 2013 refinement of N700. It is documented context here without a separate record.

A second branch from N700 reaches the underlying line. The Series N700’s tilt controller used position data from the 2006 automatic train-control upgrade on the existing Tōkaidō Shinkansen, which originally opened in 1964 (shinkansen-series-n700 → tokaido-shinkansen-2006-train-control → tokaido-shinkansen-high-speed-rail). The demonstrated connection is to the line’s signalling upgrade and the N700’s tilt function.

Taiwan’s earlier 700T came from Japan’s Series 700 through a separate procurement and adaptation (taiwan-high-speed-rail-700t → shinkansen-series-700). The N700ST continued the 700T’s livery and naming convention, while the documented source of the newer train’s engineering design was the N700S.
alternatives: Proposed in Japan: on 16 October 2026 JR Central announced its S0 series for the Tōkaidō and San’yō Shinkansen, with service planned for July 2029 and an N700S-like design configurable to multiple train lengths. The release documents an announcement and proposed entry date (JR Central press release, p. 1, https://jr-central.co.jp/news/release/_pdf/000046070.pdf).

Taiwan High Speed Rail plans to run the two Taiwanese generations together and reported completing Taipei Station platform-door modifications for their different door positions (THSRC, 28 April 2026, platform compatibility paragraphs, https://www.thsrc.com.tw/ArticleContent/c7fbf123-d806-4d25-86f7-133702a15b59).
frontier: What do railway engineers’ drawings and test reports show about the specific technologies transferred from Japan’s Series 300 and the 300X test train to Series 700? JR Central’s 2015 guide identifies both the broad lineage and test-derived knowledge, but does not specify the individual systems that carried over.

Which original Tōkaidō track and signalling constraints persisted through later renewals? Follow the engineering change records for cant and signalling, and cross-check the supplier accounts before linking earlier railway or control systems.
What results will THSRC and the Taiwanese regulator release from the subsequent N700ST main-line test stages and passenger-service authorization?
screen: Checked transport discoveries, rail-related source IDs and leads, and the existing Tōkaidō Shinkansen record’s opening and loan events. It is the existing route node and is reused. The new records are rolling-stock generations or an identifiable signalling improvement. No overlapping promoted lead was found.
coverage: Selected steel-wheel passenger services on the Tōkaidō–San’yō and Taiwan routes. Operator, manufacturer and regulator evidence was checked through 17 November 2026. The inventory reports dated operation or testing and region-specific observations, and gives proposed dates separately. Mainland China, Korea and other Japanese corridors are outside this bounded comparison.
